record.paper_title: The True Prosoluble Completion of a Group: Examples and Open Problems
record.original_question: Let Gamma be the first Grigorchuk group, identified with its image in its profinite completion PF(Gamma), which also coincides in this setting with its pro-2 completion, true prosoluble completion, and usual prosoluble completion. Does there exist an element g in PF(Gamma) \ Gamma such that the subgroup Delta generated by Gamma and g inside PF(Gamma) has the congruence subgroup property, meaning that every normal subgroup N of Delta is of the form M intersect Delta for some open normal subgroup M of PF(Gamma)? Producing such an element would give a new example of a non-isomorphic homomorphism psi: Gamma -> Delta whose induced map on profinite completions PF(psi) is an isomorphism.

evidence.quote: (4.G) Say that a subgroup ∆ of a profinite group G has the congruence subgroup property if any normal subgroup N of ∆ is of the form N = M ∩ ∆ for some open normal subgroup M of G.

(4.H) Let G be a finitely generated profinite group, and ∆ a dense subgroup of G. Let ψ : ∆ −→ G denote the inclusion. As in (4.G), the corresponding continuous homomorphism P F (∆) −→ G is always onto, and it is an isomorphism if and only if ∆ has the congruence subgroup property.
Open problem. Let Γ be the first Grigorchuk group; it is an infinite group which is residually a finite 2–group, and all its proper quotients are finite 2–groups.
The problem is to find an element g in the complement of Γ in P F (Γ) such that the subgroup ∆ of P F (Γ) generated by Γ and g has the congruence subgroup property.
This would provide one more example of a homomorphism ψ : Γ −→ ∆ which is not an isomorphism and which would be such that the homomorphism P F (ψ) is an isomorphism,
namely one solution to the original Grothendieck problem of a different nature than the existing ones (from [PlaTa–86], [PlaTa–89], and [BriGr–04]).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Gamma$ denote the first Grigorchuk group, the infinite, finitely generated, residually finite 2-group acting on the rooted infinite binary tree introduced by Grigorchuk. Let $\widehat{\Gamma}$ denote its profinite completion (which in this case coincides with its pro-2 completion, its true prosoluble completion, and its usual prosoluble completion). Identify $\Gamma$ with its (dense) image in $\widehat{\Gamma}$ via the canonical embedding.

Say that a (dense) subgroup $\Delta$ of a profinite group $G$ has the congruence subgroup property in $G$ if every normal subgroup $N$ of $\Delta$ has the form $N = M \cap \Delta$ for some open normal subgroup $M$ of $G$.

Question: Does there exist an element $g \in \widehat{\Gamma} \setminus \Gamma$ such that the abstract subgroup $\Delta = \langle \Gamma, g \rangle \le \widehat{\Gamma}$ has the congruence subgroup property in $\widehat{\Gamma}$?

(Equivalently, exhibiting such a $g$ would produce a strictly larger dense subgroup $\Delta \supsetneq \Gamma$ in $\widehat{\Gamma}$ for which the inclusion $\Gamma \hookrightarrow \Delta$ induces an isomorphism of profinite completions $\widehat{\Gamma} \xrightarrow{\sim} \widehat{\Delta}$, giving a non-isomorphic homomorphism whose profinite completion is an isomorphism.)
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not turn up any published resolution of this problem. Recent work on Grothendieck pairs and profinite rigidity (e.g., Jaikin-Zapirain–Lubotzky 2024) does not address this specific question about the first Grigorchuk group. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Some remarks on Grothendieck pairs
status_evidence.snippet: Paper on Grothendieck pairs and profinite rigidity dedicated to Grigorchuk; does not address the congruence subgroup property question for elements of PF(Grigorchuk)\Gamma.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work on Grothendieck pairs does not resolve this specific Grigorchuk-group problem.

status_evidence.title: Profinite completion of Grigorchuk's group is not finitely presented
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the structure of the profinite completion of the Grigorchuk group, showing it is not finitely presented as a profinite group, but does not address the existence of g extending Gamma with the congruence subgroup property.
status_evidence.claim: Known structural results on PF(Grigorchuk) do not settle the question.
